evals.prompt: Using the design-diagrams skill, I need a diagram for how 4 factions each play differently against 3 terrain types in my game. What diagram should I use and what's the recipe?
evals.expected: The skill picks the top-down matrix (row axis = factions, column axis = terrain), states the axes first, and emits the JSON/SVG matrix recipe, not a flowchart or triangle.
checks: the response names 'matrix' or 'top-down matrix' as the diagram type
the response names both axes explicitly (factions and terrain) before describing cells
no flowchart or relationship-triangle recipe is offered as the primary answer

evals.prompt: Using the design-diagrams skill, review this idea: draw our 5 difficulty tiers as a circle so players can loop back to an easier tier at any time. Is that the right diagram?
evals.expected: The skill runs the wrong-metaphor check, flags that a circle folds a one-dimensional difficulty continuum and can place distant tiers next to each other, and recommends a labeled linear or time-and-space diagram instead.
checks: the response explicitly names the 'wrong metaphor' check
the response identifies that a circular layout folds/hides the linear difficulty relationship
the response recommends an alternative (linear or time-and-space) diagram

evals.prompt: Using the design-diagrams skill, diagram the moment-to-moment loop: player throws a ball, dog fetches it, dog returns it, player throws again.
evals.expected: The skill picks a flowchart (engine loop) and emits a Mermaid flowchart template with player action, system response, feedback and next decision nodes.
checks: the response emits a mermaid flowchart code block
the loop closes back to the first node (a repeating cycle, not a one-way sequence)
